name: Warpriest Dragon Priest
body:
The dragon priest is a warpriest from an ancient temple devoted to draconic studies and martial arts. They are a devout warrior, whose sacred weapon is the power they harness within.

All of the following are class features of the dragon priest archetype.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

Dragon priests are proficient with the club, crossbow (light or heavy), dagger, handaxe, javelin, kama, nunchaku, quarterstaff, sai, short sword, shortspear, shuriken, siangham, sling, spear, and any weapon with the monk special weapon quality. They are also proficient with their deity’s favored weapon, and grant that weapon the monk special weapon quality if it doesn’t already have it.

Dragon priests are not proficient with any armor or shields.

When wearing armor, using a shield, or carrying a medium or heavy load, a dragon priest loses his AC bonus, as well as his sacred weapon and sacred armor abilities.

AC Bonus

When unarmored and unencumbered, the dragon priest adds his Wisdom bonus (if any) to his AC and CMD. In addition, a dragon priest gains a +1 bonus to AC and CMD at 5th level. This bonus increases by 1 at 9th, 13th, 17th, and 20th level, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks or when the dragon priest is flat-footed. He lose these bonuses when he is immobilized or helpless, when he wear any armor, when he carry a shield, or when he carry a medium or heavy load.

Blessings (Su)

A dragon priest gains 1 blessing at 1st level, and a second at 5th. They gain both of their major blessings at 9th level, instead of 10th.

This alters the progression of the warpriest’s blessings.

Sacred Weapon (Su)

At 1st level, a dragon priest can grant a +1 enhancement bonus to their sacred weapon for up to 4 rounds per day.

These rounds need not be consecutive.

A dragon priest’s sacred weapon damage increases at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter. At 20th level, it increases to 2d10 (2d8 if Small, 4d8 if Large).

At 5th level, a dragon priest’s sacred weapon counts as both cold iron and silver when overcoming Damage Reduction.

At 11th level, a lawful dragon priest counts their sacred weapon as axiomatic, and a chaotic dragon priest counts it as anarchic. A neutral dragon priest can choose either when they draw their sacred weapon, but can’t change that decision without spending 1 week in meditation to do so.

At 17th level, a dragon priest’s sacred weapon counts as adamantine when overcoming Damage Reduction and bypassing hardness.

This alters sacred weapon.

Unarmed Strike (Ex)

Dragon priests gain Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat, and they can make unarmed strikes with any part of their body, even when their hands are full.

Evasion (Ex)

At 3rd level, a monk can avoid damage from many area-effect attacks. If a monk succeeds at a Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, he instead take no damage. Evasion can be used only if a monk is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless monk does not gain the benefit of evasion.

Ki Powers

At 5th level, a dragon priest gains one ki power of their choice, as a monk of their warpriest level. They gain additional ki powers at 8th, 11th, 14th, and 17th level. If a power gained this way requires the dragon priest to spend ki points, they can use that power once per day (as if they had 1 dedicated ki point to spend), and they can spend fervor to use them again thereafter.

Individual powers may have their own limit on how many times they can be used.

The following ki powers complement the dragon priest archetype: floating breath, high jump, leap and bound, slow fall, titan leap, vertical sacred weapon strike, and wind jump.

Improved Evasion (Ex)

At 10th level, a monk’s evasion ability improves. He still take no damage on successful Reflex saving throws against attacks, but henceforth he take only half damage on failed saves. A helpless monk does not gain the benefit of improved evasion.
